comparisonPages.hub.metadata.title: CapRover vs Coolify, Dokploy and Dokku
comparisonPages.hub.metadata.description: See why developers choose CapRover for a focused, self-hosted Docker platform with a web dashboard, NGINX control, one-click apps and Docker Swarm scaling.
comparisonPages.hub.hero.title: Start simple. Never hit a ceiling.
comparisonPages.hub.hero.intro: CapRover gives you the easy path for everyday deployments and direct access to the underlying NGINX and Docker configuration when an advanced workload needs it. Run your apps, not a platform team.
comparisonPages.hub.resourceDescription: CapRover documents a 1 GB RAM minimum. Coolify and Dokploy each document 2 GB RAM and 30 GB of free storage, leaving CapRover with a lower published starting requirement.
comparisonPages.hub.shortVersion.title: CapRover keeps the common path easy without removing advanced control.
comparisonPages.hub.shortVersion.descrip: The table emphasizes concrete capabilities that support that promise. Short notes identify prerequisites and important limitations without turning every cell into a competitor brochure.

comparisonPages.coolify.metadata.title: CapRover vs Coolify: Simple Without Giving Up Control
comparisonPages.coolify.metadata.descrip: Compare CapRover and Coolify across simplicity, server requirements, deployment, Docker Swarm, NGINX, registries, rollback and advanced control.
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.title: Choose the simpler path without giving up control.
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.intro: CapRover keeps the everyday workflow focused on apps, domains and deployments. When an edge case appears, it lets you reach the underlying NGINX and Docker configuration instead of forcing you to adopt a broader platform model upfront.
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover for a lighter documented starting requirement, a standard Docker Swarm runtime, direct local deployment and deep infrastructure escape hatches. Consider Coolify when first-class Compose, independent remote servers, preview deployments or granular team workflows are mandatory.
comparisonPages.coolify.resourceDescript: CapRover documents a 1 GB RAM minimum. Coolify documents at least 2 GB RAM, 2 CPU cores and 30 GB of free storage.
comparisonPages.coolify.capabilityTitle: Focused defaults, with control available when it matters.
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.1.feature: Officially documented minimum of 1 GB RAM
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.2.feature: Purpose-built deployment from a local CLI
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.4.feature: Multi-node orchestration in the standard runtime
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.5.feature: One-click rollback without an external registry
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.7.feature: Simple dashboard with an advanced proxy escape hatch
comparisonPages.coolify.rows.8.feature: Simple dashboard with a native orchestrator escape hatch
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.title: One understandable runtime
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.parag: CapRover starts with Docker Swarm even on one server. Applications, replicas, routing and worker nodes remain part of the same model as the installation grows.
Daily work stays centered on applications rather than a hierarchy of projects, environments, resources and connected servers.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.title: Convenience without lock-in
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.parag: Use the dashboard for domains, HTTPS, variables, volumes, logs and replicas. Deploy directly with caprover deploy, upload an archive, use an image or connect a generic Git webhook.
The easy path does not remove access to Docker or NGINX when a workload needs specialized behavior.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.title: Advanced only when you ask for it
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.parag: CapRover generates working NGINX configuration automatically. If needed, the complete per-app template can be edited for redirects, headers, caching, authentication and other directives.
Native Docker service settings are also available as an advanced override, while remaining invisible to ordinary deployments.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.title: The practical difference
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.parag: Coolify covers a broader collection of projects, environments, Compose workloads and independently connected servers.

CapRover is intentionally narrower on the common path. It is a strong fit when the goal is to deploy Dockerized applications simply, retain deep control and avoid operating a larger control plane than the workload requires.
You want a simple application model with a lower documented server minimum.
You want easy defaults without losing access to NGINX and native Docker settings.
You deploy directly from your computer without requiring a Git-provider integration.
Your scaling path is one standard Docker Swarm rather than several unrelated hosts.
A platform-provisioned local registry and self-contained rollback are valuable.
comparisonPages.coolify.choice.competito: First-class Docker Compose is a primary requirement.
One control plane must manage several independent servers.
Projects, environments, preview deployments or granular team roles are required.
comparisonPages.coolify.migrationDescrip: Convert Compose services into CapRover applications or a compatible One-Click template, map domains and environment variables, and migrate persistent data with the database or storage system's own backup tooling.
comparisonPages.dokploy.metadata.title: CapRover vs Dokploy: Proven Simplicity and Deep Control
comparisonPages.dokploy.metadata.descrip: Compare CapRover and Dokploy across simplicity, server requirements, Docker Swarm, deployment, NGINX, Traefik, registries, rollback and Compose.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.title: Choose the proven, focused path to Docker Swarm.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.intro: CapRover has made Docker Swarm and NGINX approachable through an app-centric dashboard since 2017. Common deployments stay simple, while native infrastructure controls remain available for advanced workloads.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover for a lower documented starting requirement, established project history, self-contained rollback, a provisioned local registry and the combination of simple defaults with deep NGINX and Docker control. Consider Dokploy when first-class Compose, independent remote servers or multi-user workflows are required.
comparisonPages.dokploy.resourceDescript: CapRover documents a 1 GB RAM minimum. Dokploy documents at least 2 GB RAM and 30 GB of free storage for a smooth installation experience.
comparisonPages.dokploy.capabilityTitle: Two Swarm platforms, with different design priorities.
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.1.feature: Officially documented minimum of 1 GB RAM
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.2.feature: Purpose-built deployment from a local CLI
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.4.feature: Docker Swarm as the standard runtime
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.5.feature: One-click rollback without an external registry
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.7.feature: Simple dashboard with an advanced proxy escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokploy.rows.8.feature: Simple dashboard with a native orchestrator escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.title: A small application model
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.parag: CapRover keeps the core vocabulary compact: applications, domains, environment variables, persistent directories and replicas.
That focused model has remained consistent from single-server installations to multi-node Swarms, reducing the number of platform concepts required for daily operations.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.title: Self-contained deployment workflow
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.parag: Deploy source from the CLI or dashboard, use a prebuilt image, or trigger a deployment with a generic Git webhook. CapRover stores source deployment history for one-click rebuild and redeployment.
When a multi-node cluster needs a registry, CapRover can provision and manage the local registry used by the Swarm.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.title: Power without upfront complexity
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.parag: CapRover creates working NGINX and Docker service configuration automatically, so normal deployments never need to touch either.
Advanced workloads can still edit the complete per-app NGINX template and override native Docker service settings from the dashboard.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.title: The practical difference
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.parag: Dokploy makes Compose, remote servers and multi-user organizations more central to its product model.
CapRover stays focused on operating applications inside one Docker Swarm. That narrower common path is an advantage when those broader abstractions are not actual requirements.
You want an established application platform with a lower documented server minimum.
You value simple defaults and direct access to NGINX and native Docker settings.
Rollback should work without configuring an external registry.
The platform should be able to provision the local registry used by its Swarm.
Your deployment model is one understandable Docker Swarm.
comparisonPages.dokploy.choice.competito: Docker Compose and Docker Stack are primary deployment formats.
You need organizations, multiple users or role-based access.
Independent remote deployment servers or dedicated build servers are required.
comparisonPages.dokploy.migrationDescrip: Split complex Compose projects into CapRover applications or validate them against the supported One-Click fields. Map domains and environment variables, then transfer persistent data with the database or storage system's own migration tooling.
comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.title: CapRover vs Dokku: Open-Source Dashboard and CLI
comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.descripti: Compare CapRover and Dokku across simplicity, server requirements, open-source dashboards, deployment, Docker orchestration, NGINX, one-click apps and rollback.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.title: Get a complete open-source dashboard without giving up the command line.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.intro: CapRover makes the normal path visual and straightforward, while keeping CLI, API, NGINX and Docker controls available when needed. You do not have to choose between ease of use and infrastructure access.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover when dashboard operations, One-Click Apps, rollback and multi-node orchestration should be included in the open-source product. Consider Dokku when a CLI-first workflow, broad builder selection, cron and a composable plugin system are central requirements.
comparisonPages.dokku.resourceDescriptio: Both CapRover and Dokku document a 1 GB minimum with their default Docker-based runtimes. CapRover includes its web dashboard and Docker Swarm model at that published starting requirement.
comparisonPages.dokku.capabilityTitle: Visual operations and CLI deployment in the same open-source product.
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.1.feature: Officially documented minimum of 1 GB RAM
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.2.feature: Purpose-built deployment from a local CLI
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.4.feature: Multi-node orchestration in the standard runtime
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.6.feature: Simple dashboard with an advanced proxy escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.7.feature: Simple dashboard with a native orchestrator escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.title: The dashboard is the simple path
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.paragra: Domains, certificates, environment variables, persistent directories, replicas, logs and deployment history are visible and editable without assembling commands.
That makes routine operations approachable for every developer who can access the CapRover dashboard.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.title: The command line is still there
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.paragra: Run caprover deploy from a local project, upload an archive, deploy an image or trigger a generic Git webhook. The dashboard itself uses CapRover's HTTP API.
CapRover adds a visual workflow without taking away automation or terminal-based deployment.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.title: Simple does not mean limited
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.paragra: Most apps use the generated NGINX and Docker configuration unchanged. Advanced workloads can edit the complete per-app NGINX template and override native Docker service settings.
These controls stay out of the common path until an operator deliberately needs them.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.title: The practical difference
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.paragra: Dokku's open-source core is intentionally CLI-first and highly composable through builders, commands and plugins. Dokku Pro adds its official web interface and API separately.
CapRover includes its visual operations workflow, One-Click catalog and Swarm management directly in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.0: A full web dashboard should be included in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.1: You want a simple visual workflow and direct local deployment together.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.2: You want deep NGINX and Docker controls available without making them the default workflow.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.3: Docker Swarm clustering and rollback should be managed through the same product.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.4: You rely on a one-click catalog of deployable applications and databases.
SSH commands and Git push should be the primary interface.
Buildpacks and a composable plugin system are essential.
You need built-in cron task definitions or global environment variables.
comparisonPages.dokku.migrationDescripti: Convert Dokku configuration into CapRover environment variables and application settings, add captain-definition files, map domains, and migrate datastore contents with the database's own backup and restore tools.
